test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 21 March, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'** i.e. **'Weighs'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word to fill in blank number 5 is option 2: **"weighs".**
 
• In this context,** "weighs"** is used to specify the weight of the Bosavi woolly rat.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'According to the Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) there are more than 60 species of rat, which means they come in all sizes. They are typically 5 inches (12 centimeters), or longer, according to Encyclopedia Britannica. The largest species is the Bosavi woolly rat, which was discovered in 2009 in the rainforest of Papua New Guinea (and doesn't have a scientific name yet). It is about the size of a cat - 32.2 inches (82 cm) from nose to tail and **weighs** around 3.3 lbs. (1.5 kilograms), according to CNN.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are not as suitable:
 
 
• **"Evaluates" **- This term is generally used when forming an opinion or making a judgement about something. It doesn't fit in this context because we are discussing physical measurements, not judgments or evaluations.
 
• **"Counts"** - This term refers to the act of determining the total number of something, which isn't applicable in the context of discussing weight.
 
• **"Measures" **- While this term is often used to discuss dimensions or quantities, it's not typically used to refer to weight. In English, we typically say an object "weighs" a certain amount, not that it "measures" a certain amount in weight.
